item.title: Stephanie Lamprea and Alistair MacDonald Are Mesmerizing
item.description: Ecstatic Visions is an ambitious interpretation of new and recent compositions from the unique duo of Stephanie Lamprea and Alistair MacDonald.

item.title: Revisiting Drive-By Truckers’ ‘Decoration Day’ Is Rewarding
item.description: Decoration Day was the album that proved Drive-By Truckers weren't going to be a flash in the pan. It's a triumph from start to finish.

item.title: Congratulations Show Potential on the Patchy ‘Join Hands’
item.description: Potential comes in many forms, and for congratulations, it stems from the musicianship: high and mighty, stealth and singular.

item.title: Smashing Pumpkins Deliver on Grunge and Grandeur
item.description: Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness was a huge triumph in 1995, elevating the Smashing Pumpkins to global icons during their 1996 world tour.

item.title: Depeche Mode’s “Stripped” Encapsulates Analog to Algorithmic Longing
item.description: In future generations, it is easy to see Depeche Mode's "Stripped" inspiring the same sensual viscerality as humans being penetrated by their AI sex dolls.

item.title: Barry Walker Jr.’s Pedal Steel Roams an Ethereal Pasture
item.description: Barry Walker Jr.'s songs are at once somber and celebratory; they sound like a constant soundtrack to discovery, rebirth, or a hard-won peace.

item.title: Cellist Tomeka Reid Creates Dancing String Band Jazz
item.description: Tomeka Reid's music is full of the elements that have always made it fun to hear: a groove, memorable melodies, collective spirit, and conversation.

item.title: ‘Josephine’ Crawls Under Your Skin and Stays
item.description: With crime drama Josephine, Beth de Araújo has crafted a film that first and foremost doesn’t need to be reckoned with so much as sat with.

item.title: Jon Hopkins Goes Back to Nature with ‘Wilding’
item.description: Jon Hopkins and Biggi Hilmars' soundtrack, Wilding, achieves something modest but meaningful — music that makes space for the land to breathe.

item.title: What Gen X Thinks of Millennial Metalheads
item.description: One of the strangest things about being a Millennial in heavy music is realizing that you are basically Gen X's baby goth.
